one_liner: Solo-built Phaser 3 / Capacitor Android tactics game with Firebase async multiplayer, in pre-release for Google Play (internal testing).
problem: Taking a feature-complete app through store compliance, asset size and multiplayer reliability to a releasable build.
approach: Versioned release checklists and a data-safety inventory; scripted PNG to WebP asset migration; seeded deterministic combat with an append-only Firestore action log enabling replay; mission, placement and clearance validators.
decision_relevance: Shows disciplined delivery: measured optimization, compliance tracking and auditable state.

headline_results.claim: Assets reduced 72.3 MB to 6.3 MB via WebP
headline_results.evidence: git blob sums of public/assets: 72.3 MiB at ee1c5cd^ to 6.1 MiB at ee1c5cd; du now 6.3M; scripts/optimize-assets.mjs
npm run validate run 2026-09-17: missions and placements clean; clearance 1 cosmetic warning
v1.4.13 checklist open with blockers B1/B2; last AAB 1.4.11; CHANGELOG says FB login is gated 'until the app is publicly listed on the Play Store'

limitations: Not publicly listed; 1.4.13 AAB not built
No unit/integration test framework; QA is validators plus manual smoke tests
FCM Cloud Function deploy and live push unverified
No remote backup of repo or keystore
blockers_before_featuring: Recapture screenshots (current ones show pre-rebrand branding)
Keep repo private; never publish IP_REVIEW_BRIEF.md, THRENODY_REBRAND*.md, TECHDEBT.md, or Iron Tide screenshots/zip
Present as a written case study with no repo link
